PART I
Item 1. Business
Kestrel Dynamics, Inc. designs and manufactures precision motion-control systems for industrial automation customers in the U.S. and Europe. Our products are sold through direct sales teams and a network of distributors. For a discussion of the risks that could affect our business, see Part I, Item 1A, “Risk Factors,” of this Annual Report on Form 10-K.
Item 1A.  Risk Factors
Risks Related to Our Business
Our operating results depend on a limited number of large industrial customers. In fiscal 2025, our three largest customers accounted for approximately 41% of net revenue. The loss of, or a significant reduction in orders from, any of these customers could adversely affect our revenue, results of operations and financial condition, and we may be unable to replace such revenue in a timely manner.
We rely on a small number of suppliers for specialized semiconductors and rare-earth magnets. Disruption in the supply of these components, including shortages caused by geopolitical tensions, export restrictions or natural disasters, could delay shipments to customers and increase our costs. We do not have long-term supply agreements with several of these suppliers.SECRETHIDDENSPAN
Our international operations expose us to risks associated with foreign currency fluctuations, changes in tariffs and trade policies between the U.S. and other countries, and compliance with anti-corruption laws. A strengthening of the U.S. dollar relative to the euro would reduce the reported value of our European revenue and could negatively impact our operating margins.
Risks Related to Legal and Regulatory Matters
We are subject to litigation and regulatory investigations in the ordinary course of business, including product liability claims and intellectual property disputes. In 2025, a competitor, Brightline Robotics Inc. filed a lawsuit alleging patent infringement. An unfavorable outcome could require us to pay substantial damages or redesign certain products, which could harm our business.
Breaches of our information technology systems, including ransomware attacks, could disrupt our manufacturing operations, result in the loss of confidential information and expose us to regulatory penalties. Although we maintain security controls and insurance coverage, these measures may not be sufficient to prevent or fully compensate for all such incidents.

Changes in tax laws, including the adoption of a global minimum tax, could increase our effective tax rate. Our effective tax rate is also affected by the geographic mix of our earnings, and earnings that are lower than anticipated in jurisdictions with lower statutory rates could adversely affect our net income.
Item 1B. Unresolved Staff Comments
None.
Item 1C. Cybersecurity
We maintain a cybersecurity risk management program overseen by the Audit Committee of our Board of Directors and led by our Chief Information Security Officer.
Item 2. Properties
Our headquarters and principal manufacturing facility are located in Dayton, Ohio, in a leased building of approximately 180,000 square feet.
PART II
ITEM 7 — MANAGEMENT’S DISCUSSION AND ANALYSIS OF FINANCIAL CONDITION AND RESULTS OF OPERATIONS
The following discussion should be read together with our consolidated financial statements and related notes included in Item 8 of this report.
Overview
Net revenue increased 12% to $1,234.5 million in fiscal 2025, driven by strong demand for our servo drive platform and successful expansion in Europe. Gross margin improved to 38.2% from 36.5% due to favorable product mix and manufacturing efficiency gains.

Operating expenses rose 8% primarily due to higher research and development spending. Restructuring charges of $14.2 million related to the consolidation of our Mexico facility reduced operating income. We expect continued headwinds from tariffs on imported components in fiscal 2026.
Liquidity and Capital Resources
As of December 31, 2025, we had cash and cash equivalents of $312.8 million. We believe that our existing cash and available borrowing capacity will be sufficient to meet our working capital and capital expenditure needs for at least the next twelve months.
ITEM 7A. QUANTITATIVE AND QUALITATIVE DISCLOSURES ABOUT MARKET RISK
We are exposed to interest rate and foreign currency exchange rate risk.
